claims.text: Conventional HEA intermediate layers used in plasma-facing reactor components have limited heat-transfer performance.
Conventional HEA intermediate layers have marginal structural stability under high thermal and cyclic loading.
Advanced thermomechanical processing can refine the grain size of HEAs.
Advanced thermomechanical processing, including additive-manufacturing-assisted treatments, can optimize precipitate dispersion in HEAs.
Refined grain boundaries and coherent-precipitate distributions jointly mediate thermal transport and mechanical strength.
The refined microstructure reduces phonon scattering.
Reduced phonon scattering increases the thermal conductivity of the HEA intermediate layer.
A controlled dispersion of precipitates maintains or enhances the alloy's mechanical integrity.
Advanced thermomechanical processing will improve heat-transfer ability relative to conventionally processed intermediate layers.
The processed layers will preserve mechanical strength under harsh reactor thermal and mechanical conditions.
The processed layers will preserve fatigue resistance under cyclic reactor loading.
The proposed benefits will hold under high heat flux, cyclic mechanical loading, and extreme reactor operating temperatures.
Excessive grain refinement or precipitate formation caused by off-optimal processing may embrittle the alloy.
Existing literature on advanced processing routes supports the proposed mechanism.

Failure to obtain a statistically significant thermal-conductivity increase while keeping tensile strength and fatigue life within 10% of the conventional baseline is designated as a falsifying result.
